title: War Risk for Businesses Will Mean Higher Prices No Matter What Happens
partialText: Doing business in a more dangerous and unpredictable world will cost more, pushing up the price of everything from food to electronics.

title: U.S. War Against Iran Enters a New Phase
partialText: As President Trump resumes his war, the focus is now on the Strait of Hormuz. But it remains unclear how far the U.S. military will go to exert control.

title: For Israel, the U.S.-Iran Hostilities Have Created an Uneasy Limbo
partialText: Officials see a return to full-blown war as preferable to an agreement that fails to curb the threats Iran poses to Israel. Meanwhile, they wait.

title: Trump’s Latest Nominee for C.D.C. Director Will Face Senate Panel
partialText: Dr. Erica Schwartz supports vaccines and is seen as a mainstream choice to lead an agency that has been a target of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s efforts to change federal immunization policies.

title: Trump Pressures ICE to Resume Traffic Stops After They Were Halted Over Fatal Shootings
partialText: Immigration and Customs Enforcement ordered its officers on Tuesday to halt most vehicle stops across the country after they shot two people over the past week.

title: Colombian Immigrant Killed by ICE in Maine Had Legal Status, Father Says
partialText: The father of Joan Sebastian Guerrero, the man fatally shot by a federal immigration agent on Monday, said his son had been working two jobs to support his wife and daughter.

title: Videos Detail Moments Surrounding Fatal ICE Shooting in Biddeford, Maine
partialText: Footage obtained by The New York Times shows ICE agents in the moments before and after the killing of Joan Sebastian Guerrero. The circumstances of the shooting remain unclear.

title: Ukraine Pounds Russian Ships in Its Campaign to Cut Off Crimea
partialText: After striking roads and railways, Kyiv is now focusing on sea routes as it tries to disrupt fuel supplies and pressure Russia to end the war.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Review: Passion in Every Frame
partialText: Few directors close the divide between the art film and the blockbuster like Christopher Nolan.

title: Archaeologists Unearth a 2,400-Year-Old Sanctuary for the Worship of Odysseus
partialText: The ruins of a 2,400-year-old complex suggest that, to the Greeks of antiquity, Homer’s protagonist was not just a character in a poem but a figure of genuine devotion.

title: Cyclospora Was Already Hard to Investigate. Funding Cuts Make It Harder.
partialText: The parasite, which has sickened thousands across the U.S., is notoriously difficult to track. Funding cuts haven’t made the job easier.

title: How to Stay Safe From Cyclospora, a Parasite Causing Severe Intestinal Illness
partialText: Cyclospora, a parasite that causes intestinal illness, is sickening many people across the United States. Health experts have tips for avoiding infection.

title: He Thought He Had to Break Out of Brooklyn. Instead, He Celebrates It.
partialText: As a child, Michael McLeer wanted to be like John Travolta in “Saturday Night Fever” and leave the neighborhood. Was it a tragedy that changed his mind?

title: Should Epstein’s Friends Be Punished? An Elite Harvard Club Is Torn.
partialText: At Harvard, students, alumni and professors debate whether a storied campus group should cut ties with one of Jeffrey Epstein’s closest associates, and whether Harvard itself should do the same.

title: Goldman’s Former Top Lawyer Calls Epstein a ‘Masterful Liar’
partialText: Kathryn Ruemmler, the former general counsel of Goldman Sachs, testified on Wednesday in a closed-door congressional hearing investigating Jeffery Epstein.

title: The Big Questions About Jeffrey Epstein: What The Times Has Learned
partialText: Here is what we know about the sexual predator whose secrets spurred an international reckoning over money, power and complicity. Check back for updates.

title: Senator Mark Kelly Amasses Nearly $25 Million Campaign War Chest
partialText: The Arizona Democrat said he had raised and given away $10 million to fellow members of his party and committees as he mulls a presidential run in 2028.

title: Elon Musk Funds Vivek Ramaswamy’s Bid for Ohio Governor Despite Their DOGE Clashes
partialText: Elon Musk gave $5 million to back Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign for Ohio governor, seemingly moving past tensions around the effort to downsize the federal work force.

title: Biden Will Release Memoir Just After the November Midterms
partialText: The former president announced that the book, “Promise Me, America,” will come out on Nov. 17, and will cover the tumultuous events of his presidency as well as his re-election bid.

title: The American E.V. Has Been Crushed. Will It Take the U.S. Auto Industry With It?
partialText: The largest U.S. automakers have backed away from electric vehicles, even as global sales are booming. The decision may make them obsolete.

title: Wildfires Rage in Ontario as Smoke Affects Toronto’s Air Quality
partialText: Air quality in Canada’s largest city was at times the worst in the world on Wednesday, as wildfires across Ontario sent smoke drifting into New York City and beyond.

title: Wildfire Smoke Spreads Across the Northeast as Temperatures Spike
partialText: A heat dome is responsible for miserably high temperatures, and it’s also helping to push smoke from wildfires to the east.

title: California Weather Shift Brings With It a Risk of Unhealthy Heat and Wildfires
partialText: Wednesday will bring some of the hottest temperatures of the year, and fire experts are warning of combustible conditions throughout the state.

title: We’re About to Find Out Whether Republican Senators Can Still Say No
partialText: Republicans should have the decency, patriotism and self-respect to vote against Mr. Blanche.

title: ‘It’s Chaos’: What New York’s Suburbs Can Tell Us About the Mood of the Country
partialText: The midterms are looming. We asked people in New York City’s suburbs how they feel about the state of America.

title: Fatal Encounters
partialText: We look at shootings by federal immigration agents.
